title: Flows and Logics of interim and advance payments :

storage.value:
The primary objective of this system is to ensure the correct conclusion of the billing process. The billing procedure will take into consideration data derived from contracts and orders. Consequently, both of these components are essential for the correct execution of the process. To create a contract or an order, it is mandatory to define its parameters in accordance with the product, service, and goods objects.

 

The process of creating interim and advance payments within Bundle 2 follows a structure that involves the collection of essential information to accurately define the contract's parameters through products and services. The primary objective of interim and advance payments is to provide customers with the option to make define upfront payments for products or services as part of the contract.

 

Interim and advance payment object contains one individual tab, where it is mandatory to specify its parameters to facilitate the correct creation of contracts. These parameters include:

  • Name: this field is mandatory and defines information related to the interim and advance payments.

  • Value type: this parameter enables users to select the calculation logic type. Options include defining a percentage based on the previous invoice amount, specifying an exact payment amount, or calculating the amount based on the chosen price component. Users can also define the value and its range, with the mandatory inclusion of the currency for the specified amount.

    • If the obligatory checkbox is selected, it signifies that in contracts containing this interim and advance payment, it is mandatory to pay the defined amount.

    • If at least one checkbox is selected, it indicates that when a contract includes multiple interim and advance payments, at least one of the must be chosen to accurately calculate the customer's total liability with the billing process.

  • Date of issue: it is mandatory to define when the interim and advance payment should be made within the contract for the selected customer. If the 'date of the month' option is chosen, the system allows for the definition of a time period or a total value if necessary.

  • Price component: when the 'value type' is defined as the 'price component' option, user can select a relevant price component on the interim and advance payment page. The system displayed only those price components that have not been associated with other objects in the system and available for selection.

  • Periodicity: this feature allows users to specify exact weeks or months when the interim and advance payment should be active. Alternatively, user can choose a yearly time period, in which case the system recognizes that the interim and advance payment should remain active for a one-year interval.

  • Issuing  for the month to the current: through this field it is possible to define when to get the an interim and advance payment. For example, if user should get an interim and advance payment in September and selects +1 option, it means that it will be calculated in October.

  • Deduction from: it is mandatory to define from which invoice should this interim and advance payment's amount be deducted

  • Payment term: it is mandatory to define payment term values within the interim and advance payment object. Payment terms sub-object aims to outline the time range or period for the payment process of the contract. User can also select the logic for calculation this time period, such as working days or calendar days.

    • Matched with the term of the standard invoice: if this checkbox is selected, it means that defining a separate payment term for the interim and advance payment is not possible. The payment process of the created object should align with the terms of the standard invoice for this interim and advance payment.

    • No interest on overdue debts: this checkbox allows users to specify that for contracts with this term, no interest should be accrued on overdue debts.

 Minimal amount for interim payment

After the full interim invoice amount is calculated (including VAT, in default currency, per existing rounding rules), the system compares the Total amount including VAT to the minimal interim payment threshold of 5 EUR.

  1. If Total amount including VAT is greater than or equal to 5 EUR, the system creates the interim invoice and related liabilities as today.

  2. If Total amount including VAT is less than 5 EUR, the system does not create the interim invoice.

This rule applies to all interim payments, including invoices generated by the billing-run interim pipeline and by Manual interim and advance payment billing runs.

 

During interim and advance payment creation:

  • When creating an interim and advance payment, completion of all required fields is mandatory.

    • After clicking the 'Create' button, the system should check frontend validation, and if an error is detected, it should be displayed in the proper field.

    • In the event of a backend error (after successful frontend validation), the system also displays an error message.

 

 

During interim and advance payment editing:

  • Interim and advance payment does not include versioning functionality and only one version of the interim and advance payment should be created.

  • If an interim and advance payment is already included in a contract or order, editing without 'Edit Locked' permission is not possible. 

  • It is possible to change all the fields parameters in the editing mode.

 

Copy functionality:

  • The interim and advance payment includes a copy functionality, accessible during both the creation and editing modes.

    • During the creation and edit mode, it's possible to select a desired interim and advance payment to create a new object. This allows for the duplication of an object with the ability to modify its parameters. In case of any errors, the system promptly provides error notifications.

    • If an object contains inactive nomenclature, while coping that object should not be copied.
